subject: Post-demo: inference costing and feature payback (MedSys)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Nora Jacobs <nora.jacobs@medsys.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: inference costing and feature payback (MedSys)

Hi Nora —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a set of asks so we can firm up a pilot + pricing path: 

Call highlights (high level)
- Two candidate features we discussed: 1) Guided chart interpretation in clinician UI (Feature A), 2) Automated patient message drafting (Feature B).
- Ballpark usage today: pilot cohort ~5k MAU; expected pilot activity concentrated in a 10% subset of users for Feature A and 25% for Feature B.
- Desired business outcomes: improve clinician throughput, reduce message drafting time, and validate monetization per-feature.

Redwood initial econ hypotheses we want to validate
- Target pricing band for evaluation: $800–$1,400 per 1M tokens (goal: stay < $1,200/1M for pilot to hit margin targets).
- Pilot duration proposed: 6 weeks with a staged ramp.
- CAC/payback target you mentioned on the call: ~9 months (we'll model at 6–12 months).

Asks / data we need from you
1) Confirm the pilot cohort size (MAU and estimated active users for each feature).
2) A rough average prompt + response token length per feature (sample logs preferred; if not available, a best-guess number is fine).
3) Any existing target $/1M tokens you want us to anchor to for the commercial proposal.
4) Procurement timeline and primary procurement contact (we'll include them in the contract loop).

Attached: inference-feature-econ-notes.pdf (short notes and example math).

If you can send the rough token estimates, Ben will run a quick per-feature costing scenario (including batching/quantization levers) and Marissa will put together a pilot SOW and workbook.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: inference-feature-econ-notes.pdf (PDF, 220 KB)]

From: Nora Jacobs <nora.jacobs@medsys.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@medsys.io>, MedSys Procurement <procurement@medsys.io>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference costing and feature payback (MedSys)

Irene —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a couple of constraints from our side: 

1) Pilot cohort: we'll start with ~5,000 clinicians overall; expect ~500 active users for Feature A and ~1,250 active users for Feature B during the pilot window.
2) Token estimates (approx): Feature A (chart interpretation) = ~2,200 tokens per active session (prompt+response avg); Feature B (message drafting) = ~450 tokens per message. Expect Feature A 2–3 sessions per active clinician/week; Feature B ~8 messages/week.
3) Budget range: procurement has signaled a pilot budget in the $8k–$12k/month range; if we can demonstrate x3 ROI in 6 months they will expand.
4) Procurement contact: procurement@medsys.io (cc'd). Rajiv (CFO) is aware and will want a simple $/1M tokens figure in the commercial.

Additional constraints: our margin target for features post-launch is ~30% gross contribution after inference cost. CAC payback target remains ~9 months.

I've attached our internal cost model for transparency.

Nora
Nora Jacobs
Head of Product — Clinical Systems | MedSys
[Attachment: MedSys-internal-cost-model.xlsx (Excel, 120 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Nora Jacobs <nora.jacobs@medsys.io>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference costing and feature payback (MedSys)

Hi Nora —

Thanks for the numbers — helpful. Quick technical cost sketch and some levers we can apply to hit the $/1M targets you mentioned.

Assumptions from your note: pilot active users (Feature A = 500, Feature B = 1,250). Using your per-session numbers, rough monthly token volumes (rounded):
- Feature A: 500 users * 2.5 sessions/week * 4.3 weeks * 2,200 tokens = ~11.9M tokens/month
- Feature B: 1,250 users * 8 messages/week * 4.3 weeks * 450 tokens = ~19.4M tokens/month
Total pilot tokens ≈ 31.3M tokens/month.

Cost sensitivity at different $/1M anchors (pre-optimizations):
- At $1,400/1M => $43.8k/mo
- At $1,000/1M => $31.3k/mo
- At $800/1M  => $25.0k/mo

Optimization levers we can apply quickly (pilot):
1) Prefix/KV caching for chart interpretation: caching repeated chart context can reduce Feature A token consumption by ~25–40% depending on reuse patterns.
2) Dynamic batching and token-size-aware routing: reduces per-token overhead during peak windows.
3) Quantization and runtime kernel tuning (INT8/INT4 where acceptable): can reduce cost per query ~20–35% with small quality checks.

If we layer realistic optimizations (conservative): expect a 35–45% reduction in effective inference spend. Applying a 40% reduction to the $1,000/1M baseline moves pilot spend closer to ~$18.8k/mo. That puts a $8k–$12k/month procurement window in reach if MedSys secures a pilot discount and we structure usage thresholds.

Per-feature example (at $1,000/1M pre-opt):
- Feature A cost = 11.9M * $1,000/1M = $11.9k/mo (pre-opt). Post-opt (~40% savings) ≈ $7.1k/mo.
- Feature B cost = 19.4M * $1,000/1M = $19.4k/mo (pre-opt). Post-opt ≈ $11.6k/mo.

Hints on CAC/payback math you asked us to model: if a feature drives $X incremental revenue per activated clinician per month, and acquisition cost per clinician is $Y, payback months = Y / (X * gross_margin_after_inference). We'll put a sample table in the workbook for three scenarios (best/mid/conservative).

Next asks from our side
- If you can share 1–2 anonymized prompt logs or a sanitized aggregate token distribution (percentiles), I can run a micro-simulation and produce a per-feature $/feature figure for the pilot.
- Any minimum SLO/latency requirements that would prevent aggressive batching/quantization?

Happy to jump on a brief tech call if Rajiv wants more detail.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Nora —

Great thread and thanks for the detail. I've pulled together a short workbook and a proposed pilot scope to make the econ explicit and to help procurement sign off. Next steps we propose: 

1) Redwood to run a quick per-feature micro-simulation once we receive a small sample of token logs (sanitized). Ben will produce per-feature $/feature and expected pilot burn bands.
2) Execute a 6-week pilot SOW (attached) with predefined KPIs: token volume, latency SLO, quality guardrails, and demo week at week 5.
3) Commercial: we'll provide a pilot discount schedule tied to monthly usage bands and a target $/1M anchor for the pilot. If the pilot meets the ROI gates we'll move to a tiered production pricing cadence.
4) Procurement: please provide the contact who will sign the SOW. We can send the initial SOW via DocuSign (link below) for a one-click acceptance.
